enonce_intro_markdown:
**SECTION B - COMPOSITION (40 marks)**

Mark distribution: Content and Organisation (12 marks); Expression (16 marks); Accuracy (12 marks).

Choose ONE topic to write on from the list below. You are advised to write clearly and effectively, to spell and punctuate correctly, and to ensure that your writing is appropriate in style and content to the topic chosen. Avoid obscene language and do not disclose your identity (e.g. your name, school, parentage etc). You should write between 450 - 500 words.

questions.enonce_markdown: **d)** Write a letter to your friend Olata who has gone abroad, giving him/her news of yourself, family and town. Your name is Senga Akata and your address is 23 Eti Road, Kambu.
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Plan**

1. Address and date at the top right, then the salutation and an opening wish.
2. News of myself: studies and activities.
3. News of the family: parents, sister and brother.
4. News of the town: new road, health centre, festival, old friends.
5. Closing request to write back, ending and signature.

**Model composition (462 words)**

23 Eti Road,
Kambu.
15th April 2022.

Dear Olata,

I hope this letter finds you in good health and high spirits. It is already six months since you left for abroad, and I have missed you a lot. Everybody here keeps asking about you, and I promised to send you all the news, so please sit down and read it slowly.

Let me begin with myself. I am doing very well, thank God. I am now in Form Five and preparing seriously for the GCE examination in June. Our teachers push us hard, and I spend most evenings at the library with Tabe and Mercy, who send you their greetings. I have also joined the school debating club, and last month we won the inter-college competition. You would have been proud to see me speaking in front of the whole school! Please tell me how your own studies are going and whether the weather there is as cold as people say.

Now to the family. Father is well, though he complains of tiredness after long days at the market, where he sells cloth. Mother has started a small poultry farm behind the house, and the chicks are growing fast; she says she will give you the first cock when you return. My elder sister, Ndi, got married in December in a beautiful ceremony, and the whole quarter came to celebrate. She has moved to Bamenda with her husband, and the house feels quiet without her. My little brother, Mbah, has lost two teeth and now whistles when he talks, which makes everybody laugh.

As for our town, a lot has changed since you left. The main road has been tarred at last, and the journey to the market that used to take thirty minutes now takes ten. A new health centre has opened near the church, so patients no longer travel to the city for simple treatment. Unfortunately, the dry season has brought a lot of dust, and the water shortage in some quarters is becoming serious. The annual cultural festival will take place next month, and the committee is already preparing dances, wrestling and a football match. I wish you could be here to join the dancers as you did last year.

Our old friends send their love. Ayuk is now working in a bank, Fanny has opened a hair salon, and Bate still asks whether you remember the mangoes we used to take from Mr Ako's tree. I told him you do!

Please write soon and send some photographs of the place where you live. I want to see your new friends and the snow, if there is any. Give my respects to the people who are taking care of you, and take care of yourself.

Yours lovingly,
Senga Akata

**Marking grid**

| Criterion | Marks | What earns the marks |
|---|---|---|
| Content and Organisation | 12 | Relevant ideas that answer the topic, developed with examples, in clear paragraphs with an introduction and a conclusion |
| Expression | 16 | Varied vocabulary and sentence structures, appropriate style and tone, fluent links between ideas |
| Accuracy | 12 | Correct grammar, tenses, spelling and punctuation |

**Common mistakes**

1. Using the wrong format: no address and date, a formal salutation or ending, or a signature other than the name given (Senga Akata).
2. Giving news about only one of the three required areas (self, family, town), or writing in a formal tone to a close friend.
